hypothesis: NTPC is effectively leveraging subsidiary structures (NGEL, NREL) to pivot toward non-fossil sources while maintaining coal as a stability mechanism.

research_questions.question: What is the historical growth rate of renewable energy (RE) capacity commissioned by NGEL and NREL vs. the parent company coal additions?
Does the revenue growth of the non-fossil segment outperform the traditional coal segment on a constant-currency basis?

evidence_ledger.excerpt_or_data_point: In FY 2024-25, our revenue from non-fossil energy sources reached 17,359.67 crore (9.33% of total revenue)
evidence_ledger.claim_supported: NTPC reports current non-fossil energy contribution

evidence_ledger.excerpt_or_data_point: As of March 31, 2025, the NTPC Group has commissioned 6.8 GW of renewable energy capacity

checklist.step: Analyze NTPC Group Annual Reports for 2020-2024
checklist.expected_evidence: Historical year-on-year RE commissioning data and coal-based generation revenue
cross_validation_sources: Ministry of Power - Central Electricity Authority (CEA) reports
checklist.completion_criteria: Successful extraction of a 5-year trend line for both RE and Coal capacities.

checklist.expected_evidence: Project-level commissioning certificates or press releases
cross_validation_sources: CERC (Central Electricity Regulatory Commission) Tariff Orders
MNRE (Ministry of New and Renewable Energy) public database
checklist.completion_criteria: Correlation of reported 6.8 GW figure with independent project registries.

alternative_explanation: Expansion is driven by state-mandated targets and capital subsidies rather than a fundamental business model pivot.
falsification_test: If generation volume from renewable sources remains flat or declines over three consecutive fiscal years despite the 14.5 GW under-execution backlog, the hypothesis of an effective pivot is invalidated.
